newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya issues warrant to arrest rebel commander.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya issues warrant to arrest rebel commander.

text.p: Russia's separatist region of Chechnya has issued an arrest warrant for radical commander Salman Raduyev after he took responsibility for two bomb attacks in southern Russia, Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday.

"Measures are being taken to find and arrest Raduyev... I think we will soon put an end to declarations which discredit the Chechen government," Tass quoted Ruslan Kutayev, an aide to Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov as saying.
Interfax news agency quoted Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev as saying his ministry had not yet received an order to arrest Raduyev.

Kutayev said the Chechen authorities did not think Raduyev was behind the bomb blasts last month at railways stations in the southern Russian towns of Armavir and Pyatigorsk, each of which killed two people.
"All that Raduyev says is the fruit of his own imagination," Kutayev said.
He reiterated that the Chechen government was convinced that the bomb blasts had been staged by Russian special services in order to dicredit the Chechen leadership.

Raduyev, a flamboyant but isolated figure who is not part of Chechnya's post-war separatist leadership, has vowed several times to attack Russian targets over Moscow's continued refusal to recognise the region's independence.
Russia halted its military campaign to crush Chechnya's secessionist drive last August and is now locked in peace talks with the separatists.

Raduyev said in a television interview broadcast by the Russian commercial channel NTV on Sunday that the explosions were carried out on his personal orders and that they heralded a new phase of the Russian-Chechen war.

Russian police have detained two Chechen women suspected of organising the Pyatigorsk blast. Raduyev said in the television interview Russia would regret it if any harm came to the two women and that he was planning further attacks in Russia.
Raduyev is also wanted by Russian police for masterminding a bloody armed raid in the Russian region of Dagestan, bordering Chechnya, in January last year.
